notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, as the town reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.

Public schools are run by a separate school district. The town's tax bill also collects the taxes for the school district and the county; residents pay all of them, but only the town's share is counted here.

The town reported $761,000 of property tax, which includes the shares it collects for the school district and the county. Only the town's own share, $506,000 (what its spending needed beyond its other revenue, which is how the town tax rate is set), is counted, so the town shows no surplus or deficit for the year.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($5,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Maine city, town and plantation candidates file campaign finance reports with their municipal clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
